solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Water fern sick wife found in dockland area (8)

indicatorNotes.found in: the sick wife is found inside the dockland area, so ILL W goes within PORT

blocks.note: a port is a docks area; it wraps the rest

annotation.surface: A sick wife turns up somewhere around the docks, beside a water fern.
annotation.walkthrough: Pillwort is a small aquatic fern with pill-shaped spore cases; the surface's hospital-case reading of 'sick wife' hides two tiny pieces going into the port.
annotation.definitionFit: Pillwort is a real fern growing in wet places, so 'Water fern' names it exactly.

entries.clue: Woman taking step to identify plains (6)

annotation.surface: A woman takes a step towards identifying a stretch of flat country.
annotation.walkthrough: PAS is the French word for step, familiar from ballet (pas de deux); the pampas are the grassy plains of South America.
annotation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast treeless plains of Argentina, so 'plains' is a straight synonym.

entries.clue: Article in seagoing vessel having one dimension (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the article sits inside the vessel

blocks.note: an ocean liner; it goes round the article

annotation.surface: A newspaper article about some ship, which apparently has only one dimension.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a piece of writing in the surface; here it is the grammatical article A.
annotation.definitionFit: Something linear extends along a line only, which is to say it has one dimension.

entries.clue: Sport, one not a little tedious (9)

blocks.note: to sport a hat is to wear it
some = a fair amount, not a little

annotation.surface: Someone finds a particular sport more than a little tedious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a noun naming a game, but it is the verb meaning to wear or show off.
annotation.definitionFit: Wearisome means tiring through dullness, the same as tedious.

entries.clue: Further tweaking involving impartial fellows badly rated externally (12)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters of RATED are put together badly, i.e. rearranged
indicatorNotes.externally: the rearranged RATED sits on the outside of JUST MEN

blocks.note: RATED rearranged, split READ…T around the middle

annotation.surface: More fiddling with the rules, because some fair-minded men were poorly rated from outside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'involving' is only a link here. 'badly rated externally' asks for a short anagram used as the outer shell, which is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to readjust is to adjust again, and tweaking is small adjustment.

entries.clue: Item left in car with sloping back (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' in its plain sense of inside: the item left is in the car, so L sits inside COUPE

blocks.note: a coupé is a two-door car with a sloping rear

annotation.surface: Something has been left behind in a fastback car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Item' is slang for a romantic couple (they're an item), not an object left in a car.
annotation.definitionFit: Two people who are 'an item' are a couple, so Item can stand for COUPLE.

entries.clue: Asian bloke arrested by call to attention (5)

indicatorNotes.arrested by: the bloke is held inside the call

blocks.note: oi! = a shout to get attention; it holds MAN

annotation.surface: A police scene: an Asian man is arrested after someone shouts at him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Asian' looks like it describes the bloke, but it is the definition on its own; OI is British slang for 'hey!'.
annotation.definitionFit: Oman is in Asia, on the Arabian Peninsula, so an Omani is an Asian.

entries.clue: Pitiful way it turns up in City district (8)

indicatorNotes.turns up: in a down clue, turning up reverses IT to TI
indicatorNotes.in: the reversed IT goes inside the City district

blocks.note: EC = the City of London's postcode district; it holds TI

annotation.surface: Some pitiful route appears in a district of the City.
annotation.walkthrough: The City (capital C) is the financial district of London, whose postcodes begin EC.
annotation.definitionFit: Pathetic and pitiful both mean arousing pity or contempt.

entries.clue: Service, say, involving archdeacon and offspring (8)

indicatorNotes.involving: 'say' takes in the archdeacon and the offspring

blocks.note: e.g. = for example, 'say'; it wraps the rest

annotation.surface: A church service with an archdeacon and some child taking part.
annotation.walkthrough: The Church of England styles an archdeacon 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven.; 'say' is the example-giver EG.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Anglican evening prayer is one kind of church service.

entries.clue: Male US attorney with place in a Buddhist centre (8)

annotation.surface: An American lawyer with a place at a Buddhist centre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'with' just strings the pieces together; 'in' joins the wordplay to the definition. Mandalay in Myanmar is a major centre of Buddhism.
annotation.definitionFit: Mandalay, the old royal capital of Burma, is full of monasteries and pagodas, a Buddhist centre.

entries.clue: Man on board thrown by deals regularly backfiring (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take every other letter of 'deals': E, L
indicatorNotes.backfiring: those letters fire backwards, giving LE

annotation.surface: A man on a boat is thrown overboard as some deals go wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor; the board is a chessboard and the man a chess piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-favourite sense: chess pieces are traditionally called men, and the rook is one of them on the board.

entries.clue: Old fish market’s scandal over presentation of accounts? (12)

blocks.note: billing = sending out accounts to customers

annotation.surface: An old fish market caught up in a scandal about how its accounts were presented.
annotation.walkthrough: 'over' reads as 'about': the answer is a scandal about billings, a billings-gate. Billingsgate was London's historic fish market.
annotation.definitionFit: Billingsgate was the City of London's fish market for centuries before moving to Docklands.

entries.clue: He made violins in the morning, very early! (5)

blocks.note: at 1 = at one o'clock, very early in the morning; 1 reads as I

annotation.surface: A violin maker who was at work first thing in the morning.
annotation.walkthrough: One o'clock in the morning is 'very early'; the digit 1 is written as the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona were celebrated violin makers of the 16th and 17th centuries.

entries.clue: Succulence mostly just in ices somehow (9)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of 'just', its last letter dropped
indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters are arranged somehow, i.e. mixed up

annotation.surface: Juiciness, it seems, is found mostly in ices.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link placing the succulence inside the ices, but it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Succulence is juiciness, the quality of being full of juice.

entries.clue: Study post covering extremely useful discussion (12)

indicatorNotes.covering: the post covers, i.e. goes round, the next piece
indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extremes of 'useful': U and L

blocks.note: a station is a post, a place of duty

annotation.surface: A study post that covers some very useful discussion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Con' is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart.
annotation.definitionFit: A consultation is a meeting to discuss something.

entries.clue: Pa’s a rogue, appalling the High Court? (9)

indicatorNotes.appalling: the letters are in an appalling state, i.e. jumbled

annotation.surface: Father is a scoundrel, which scandalises the court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'appalling' reads as an adjective describing the rogue, but it is the anagram indicator. The question mark flags the High Court as ancient Athenian.
annotation.definitionFit: The Areopagus was the highest judicial council of ancient Athens, named after the hill where it sat.

entries.clue: Southern explorer in charge of vessels finally going north — cutters (8)

indicatorNotes.going north: in a down clue, going north reverses everything before it

annotation.surface: A southern explorer takes charge of ships heading north, and the cutters too.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Southern explorer' looks like one idea but splits into S and ROSS; the whole string SROSSICS is then read upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Scissors are a cutting tool, so 'cutters' fits.

entries.clue: Arrogant fool with high-class china (8)

annotation.surface: An arrogant fool shows off expensive porcelain.
annotation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U language; 'china' is porcelain, not the country.
annotation.definitionFit: Assuming, as an adjective, means presumptuous or arrogant.

entries.clue: Street trader’s period plugging a type of eel containing bone (12)

indicatorNotes.plugging: the period plugs a gap in the eel
indicatorNotes.containing: the eel also contains the bone

blocks.note: the conger eel; it holds the rest

annotation.surface: A street trader spends a period stuffing an eel with bone.
annotation.walkthrough: A costermonger is a London barrow-seller of fruit and vegetables; 'Street trader’s' means 'Street trader is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A costermonger sells produce from a barrow in the street, a street trader.

entries.clue: Beam, seeing part of Carousel in telecast (6)

indicatorNotes.seeing part of: the answer is part of the following words

annotation.surface: A spotlight picks out a scene from the musical Carousel on television.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beam' suggests a light beam in a TV studio; it is a structural beam.
annotation.definitionFit: A lintel is the horizontal beam over a door or window.

entries.clue: Mole crossing railway line with agility (6)

indicatorNotes.crossing: the mole stretches across, i.e. around, railway and line

blocks.note: a mole is a spy planted in an organisation

annotation.surface: A mole scuttles nimbly across a railway track.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mole' suggests the burrowing animal; it is the undercover agent.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: spry means nimble, so the adverb describes moving nimbly.

entries.clue: Thus act, so to speak, getting sweet wine (9)

indicatorNotes.so to speak: said out loud, the words make the answer

blocks.note: so = thus, turn = an act on stage

annotation.surface: Performing like this, one earns some sweet wine.
annotation.walkthrough: A turn is a short act in variety theatre; Sauternes is pronounced roughly 'so-TURN'.
annotation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux.

entries.clue: Husbandless woman in compound (5)

indicatorNotes.less: the woman's name without H, husband

annotation.surface: A woman without a husband living in a walled compound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like an enclosure where she lives; it is a chemical compound. H is the standard abbreviation for husband.
annotation.definitionFit: An ester is a chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

entries.clue: Prudish people principally dress in fine clothes (5)

indicatorNotes.principally: only the principal, first letter of 'people'

annotation.surface: Prudish people above all like to dress in their finery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prudish people' reads as one phrase, but it splits: the adjective gives PRIM and 'people' only its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To primp is to dress or groom yourself carefully and smartly.

entries.clue: Old rover loses right to supply narcotic drug (6)

indicatorNotes.loses: 'loses' in its sense of parting with something: the pirate parts with its R, right

annotation.surface: An old wanderer drops out of the right side to deal drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: A rover here is a sea-rover, a pirate, not a wanderer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: drugs made from opium dull the senses and induce sleep, the core meaning of narcotic.

entries.clue: Gizmos daughters obtain in Indiana port (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the daughter and 'obtain' go inside the port

blocks.note: Gary, Indiana, a port on Lake Michigan; it wraps the rest

annotation.surface: Some daughters pick up gadgets in an Indiana port.
annotation.walkthrough: Gary is a steel town on Lake Michigan, hence a port; D stands for daughter or daughters.
annotation.definitionFit: Gadgetry is a collective word for gadgets or gizmos.

entries.clue: Retired American chap exuding sweetness (6)

indicatorNotes.Retired: retiring means going back, so US is turned round

annotation.surface: A retired American man with a charmingly sweet manner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired American chap' looks like one old man; it splits into reversed US and a chap's name, the same Gary as the port in 25 across.
annotation.definitionFit: Sugary means sweet, or cloyingly sweet in manner, exuding sweetness.

entries.clue: With support large Yankee becomes sly and treacherous (8)

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A big American, once he has backing, turns sly and treacherous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' suggests an American; it is the radio code word for Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Weaselly means like a weasel: sly, shifty and untrustworthy.
